changelog: The system now checks its own update source at every start and every update check: if it was ever left pointing somewhere other than the official release -- which silently freezes a system on its old version -- it corrects itself and carries on updating.
details: 50b (bench revision, stacked on 50a for the next bare-number release): makes v13's rescue repair permanent on the main line. A unit whose CYTECH_MANIFEST_URL is not the canonical main one cannot update at all, and neither failure looks like a failure. The retired test branch leaves it on whatever version that branch serves, reporting 'up to date' -- truthfully, relative to that frozen source -- forever. Any other ref (a release tag left behind by a service visit, a commit SHA, or no ref at all) makes cytech_update.sh build a download base that 404s, so the owner sees 'Update failed while downloading <file>. Will retry on next boot.', which never resolves. v13 (published on the test branch) reached the frozen class by rewriting the URL during Check for Update and at boot; this revision puts the same repair in first_boot.sh and cytech_check_only.sh on main, so it reaches every unit that ever gets these scripts -- including ones sealed in their box, since the boot call sits above the .zero_touch_completed branch and runs before anything reads the URL. Scope is deliberately narrow: it rewrites the URL only when the host is raw.githubusercontent.com, the repo path is exactly slychiu/ComfortHA-yaml, and the ref is something other than main (test, a tag, a SHA, or missing). A local test mirror, another repo, a nested path, a foreign host or a non-manifest path is left strictly alone -- verified by the unit suite, which also covers the surrounding shapes, a quoted value, a trailing CR, a commented-out line, an already-correct file (silent no-op, no backup) and a missing file (fresh unit, no crash). The original value is kept once in /config/.cytech_secrets.bak_pre_manifest_repair and never overwritten; a unit that already carries the v13 rescue's backup keeps it, and this line writes its own. The in-process variable is refreshed, so the very press that repairs the URL already checks against the real latest rather than waiting for the next pass. cytech_update.sh is re-shipped unchanged in the same payload: on a unit healed by the v12/v13 rescue it is still the old pre-v42-era updater, which has no tag-scoped downloads and no Core-restart triggers, so shipping the current one is what converges those units onto the fleet updater. No new entity, no dashboard change, no owner-visible screen. Bench-verified 2026-09-22 on cytech.local from the served bytes: the check offered 50b, the update landed all three files md5-identical to the tag blobs, and Core restarted. Both repair paths were then exercised live. Boot path: the URL was pinned to a release tag (/48/manifest.json, the shape a service visit leaves behind), the unit was restarted, and the boot pass repointed it to main, logged the repair, wrote the backup holding the 48 URL, left the version and every other secrets line untouched, and offered no spurious update. Check path: the URL was set to the retired test branch, and that single press both repaired the URL and reported 'System is up to date (v50b)' -- where an unrepaired unit goes on reporting 'up to date' permanently, from the old source. The narrow scope was confirmed on the bench as well: with the URL pointing at a local test mirror, a full boot pass wrote no repair line and created no backup. The unit suite (98 assertions against the function text extracted from the two committed scripts) passes on the PC and on the bench against the deployed copies, including the fleet-only deltas -- the new backup filename, the new log prefix, and a unit that already carries the v13 rescue's backup receiving its own. Not published yet -- 50b is a bench revision, stacked on 50a, and the two ship together inside the next bare-number release.
